newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian bourse buoyant after budget report.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian bourse buoyant after budget report.

text.p: Nigerian shares ended in buoyant mood on Friday as investors reacted positively to the finance minister's mid-term budget report late on Thursday.

The all-share index closed at 6,175.01 from 6,158.09 on Wednesday, the last day on which the index was updated. Over the week the index gained just over 0.55 percent. Traders said after the budget report that they were happy with government's handling of the economy in the first half of the year.
"We welcome the taming of inflation, which is bringing lower interest rates, as well as the administration's decision to repay local debts," one trader said.
They said rises in share prices are likely to continue at least in the short term, with no information suggesting that conditions are worsening.
Union Bank rose 15 kobo to 7.05 naira.

Oil shares closed generally higher. National Oil was 16 kobo higher at 27.36 naira, while Total finished 10 kobo higher at 43.12 naira. Construction firm G. Cappa gained the maximum five percent, rising 23 kobo to 4.83 naira, following the listing of its recent rights issue.
Conglomerate PZ Industries rose 15 kobo to 32.70 naira, while Lever Brothers closed 10 kobo higher at 24.30 naira.

Ashaka Cement and Benue Cement Co were five kobo up at 15 naira and 3.88 naira, respectively, while Cement Co of Northern Nigeria managed a three kobo rise to 2.32 naira. West African Portland Cement was seven kobo up at 28.02 naira.
Nigerian Breweries fell by three kobo to 13.70 naira, while Guinness dropped five kobo to 9.60 naira.
Delta Glass, CMB and Studio Press all finished two kobo lower, at 6.23 naira, 4.50 naira and 1.30 naira, respectively.
Thomas Wyatt was 35 kobo lower at 7.31 naira after adjustment for dividend. ($1=80 naira)
